reviews.text: The film ends on a note of human vulnerability I’ve simply never seen from Hopkins before and it absolutely destroyed me.
reviews.author: Bernard Ozarowski

reviews.text: It is a very physical performance: unflinching, dazzling and one so mesmerisingly upsetting that I never want to watch it again.
reviews.author: Francesca Steele

reviews.text: A psychological drama that has the originality of narrating the action from the point of view of an older man, through which the viewer must discover if he suffers from some type of senile dementia, or if it is his environment who wants harm him.
reviews.author: Denise Pieniazek

reviews.text: Trigger warning: do not watch “The Father” (2020) if you are unprepared to be completely gutted and devastated. Side effects may include life altering change in perspective and emerging fear of aging in the US.
reviews.author: Sarah Vincent

reviews.text: The Father is a film that punches you straight in the gut. You’ll never be able to forget this one.
reviews.author: Sarah Cortinaz

reviews.text: Anthony Hopkins’ Oscar-winning act leaves you with a heavy heart.
reviews.author: Pradeep Kumar

reviews.text: The great Anthony Hopkins plays Anthony, an eighty-something-year-old man who’s constantly at war with his own cognition.
reviews.author: Paul Kanieski

reviews.text: Through our protagonist’s mental condition, we witness how human consciousness turns against us. That an ill mind can make a cruel and grotesque joke about our very existence, setting up a punch line that will tear down the world we thought we lived in.
reviews.author: Akos Peterbencze

reviews.text: The Father is an overwhelmingly devastating depiction of the painfully progressive disease that is dementia. Anthony Hopkins delivers an award-worthy, powerfully compelling performance. One of the best movies I've seen in the last couple of years.
reviews.author: Manuel São Bento

reviews.text: The Father has, like his [protagonist's] mind, an elliptical structure, made of holes and voids. Allowing us to get lost and confounded in its thrilleresque atmosphere... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Anna Dodier

reviews.text: An act of empathic genius.
reviews.author: M.N. Miller

reviews.text: “The Father” is a tough watch. But the bold choices, the emotional honesty, the crisp detailed storytelling, and the tour de force performance from Anthony Hopkins (among other things) make every second worthwhile.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: The script ensnares us into the life of this man, though the audiovisual elements could've been more inspired. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Erick Estrada

reviews.text: It is not just a film that you watch, it is a film that you experience - mind, body, and soul.
reviews.author: Dan Bayer

reviews.text: Capped by one of the most harrowing speeches youll see all year, The Father belongs in that special category of films that are brilliant but may require a bit of a break before you see them again
reviews.author: Victoria Luxford

reviews.text: It's an incredibly accomplished, well-structured chamber drama, aided in its translation to English by playwright and screenwriter Christopher Hampton.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: Not only is the film absolutely affecting, but the sheer confidence that it carries would be impressive for any film much less a directorial debut.
reviews.author: Carson Timar

reviews.text: The film does what Christopher Nolan keeps trying and failing at, which is to ever so gingerly reach into our minds and tweak out the corners and meaty pieces of our perceptions, before we even notice what's being done
reviews.author: Jason Adams

reviews.text: Extraordinary. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: William Venegas

reviews.text: Director Florian Zeller makes light work of this adaption of his play, using the camera to recreate the claustrophobia and uncertainty of relying on an uncertain mind.
reviews.author: Cate Young

reviews.text: Anthony Hopkins is one of the best actors alive right now, undoubtedly. The Father was one of the best surprises of 2020, with an incredible visual concept that blows my mind when I think this is Zeller's first film. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Victor Pineyro

reviews.text: [Much] of the strength of the film lies in Anthony Hopkins' lead performance alongside Olivia Colman, Zeller's direction is nothing to sniff at.
reviews.author: Therese Lacson

reviews.text: It's a film that's worth more for its conception and execution than its ideological discourse or social agenda. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fernanda Solórzano

reviews.text: Memory is not linear, and 'The Father' captures what it must feel like when memories stop connecting. Anthony Hopkins gives one of his great performances.
reviews.author: Witney Seibold

reviews.text: The film seamlessly blends genuine fear with overwhelming sadness.
reviews.author: Anupama Chopra

reviews.text: Hopkins...has never been better. And, given his much garlanded career, that really is saying something.
reviews.author: Jason Best

reviews.text: Watching The Father feels like watching a particularly good episode of Black Mirror, without any of the tech paranoia.
reviews.author: Rohan Naahar

reviews.text: A forensic examination, powerfully written and delivered with brio, of the impact of dementia on a retired engineer and those closest to him
reviews.author: Jane Freebury

reviews.text: The word "devastating" is used so much as to be almost devalued. But, in its truest, most powerful sense, The Father is devastating.
reviews.author: Aine O'Connor

reviews.text: There is no gawdy tricks, nor leaning on tropes. From start to finish The Father is exactly what you see it as. Confusing, scary, loving, and sad.
reviews.author: Taylor Baker

reviews.text: It has an exceptional script, and not only because of the dialogues' quality, but because it plays with what the viewer sees and understands. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pablo O. Scholz

reviews.text: [Anthony Hopkins] is absolutely remarkable here. I read the screenplay, available online, out of curiosity, and what he brings to the words on the page is beyond and beyond and beyond. Hopkins has played King Lear (twice) but this is his real King Lear.
reviews.author: Deborah Ross

reviews.text: The way Zeller and his production designer Peter Francis orchestrate these changes are almost imperceptible, but nevertheless disorienting and utterly crucial to the narrative.
reviews.author: Esther Zuckerman

reviews.text: Watching two great performers together provides The Father's highpoint.
reviews.author: Robin Holabird

reviews.text: Without resorting to exploitative, amped-up mystery or obfuscation, Zeller and co-writer Christopher Hampton have fashioned a sort of gaslight thriller in which the mind is both predator and prey.
reviews.author: Guy Lodge

reviews.text: Zeller has delivered not only the best film adaptation of the season, but one of the most effective, moving and, dare I say, cinematic films of the year.
reviews.author: Catherine Springer

reviews.text: Yet The Father is a powerful debut. The mood of isolation with its warped sense of time and the distanced characters confined to their homes: this film reflects our present moment without labouring the point home or making the obvious analogies.
reviews.author: Tom Baily

reviews.text: This is a film of immeasurable power which everyone should experience once. It explores the frailties of being human, in a society which increasingly values youth over experience.
reviews.author: Martin Carr

reviews.text: With his first feature film Florian Zeller has delivered a stunning, heart-breaking and terrifying film about dementia.
reviews.author: Tom Crowley

reviews.text: The Father distorts and disorients in keeping with its protagonist's increasingly confused view of the world.
reviews.author: Tara Brady

reviews.text: The movie transmits the feeling of loss while the person is physically alive [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Gisela Savdie

reviews.text: The Father is unmissable; a haunting, delicate masterpiece that conjures incredible empathy, understanding, fear, and grief for its characters.
reviews.author: Laura Potier

reviews.text: [I]n this film love ends up winning, no matter how difficult it is. sometimes.
reviews.author: Alejandro G. Calvo

reviews.text: It's a film that disquiets on a cellular level.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: Huge plaudits are due to production designer Peter Francis, whose subtly reconfigured sets disorient the viewer, matching Anthony's increasingly bewildered experience.
reviews.author: Mark Kermode

reviews.text: It feels about as close to losing your grip as you could come - and is terrifying.
reviews.author: Dulcie Pearce

reviews.text: Whether I've convinced you to go or not, The Father is well worth all the acclaim that has been heaped upon it.
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: The Father is a moving and disorientating psychological drama that boasts another career-defining performance from the masterful Anthony Hopkins.
reviews.author: Lewis Knight

reviews.text: The Father could well be the first film to truly convey what it must feel like to be falling into the grips of dementia and is as heartbreaking as it is brilliantly innovative in a narrative sense.
reviews.author: Linda Marric

reviews.text: Hopkins is extraordinary as a man flailing against a condition that's taking everything from him. And Zeller proves he's a natural filmmaker, orchestrating a Wagnerian opera of emotion based entirely around an old man in a flat.
reviews.author: Nick De Semlyen

reviews.text: It's deeply moving, important work, whether or not it was ever destined to win awards.
reviews.author: Clarisse Loughrey

reviews.text: It is a film about grief and what it means to grieve for someone who is still alive.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: ...immaculately crafted, outwardly dispassionate, and inwardly shattering...
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: The real advantage of mediating our experience of the film largely through Hopkins' performance, though, is that we get a more robust and empathetic view of what it means for a man to confront his own mortality...
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: In its howls of mortal distress, Florian Zeller's film is as hypnotically ugly as a Francis Bacon mouth, as doom-drenched as one of Larkin's late laments.
reviews.author: Ryan Gilbey

reviews.text: The sense of control is essential. The film is such a scramble it would unravel without it. Still. All Zeller's brilliance would be for naught without Hopkins.
reviews.author: Danny Leigh

reviews.text: Anthony Hopkins' central hypnotic performance goes a long way in reassuring you that this movie deserves your complete attention.
reviews.author: Alif Majeed

reviews.text: Haunting and credible, powered by some unshakable performances.
reviews.author: Hannah Strong

reviews.text: It's not often that a film like this comes along, that feels unlike any other feature that has come before it, and that you can't imagine any viewer coming away from any less than utterly enthralled and heartbroken.
reviews.author: Deirdre Molumby

reviews.text: The Father is no cinematic event, but its empathetic, unflinching, deeply humanising look at dementia marks a high point in Hopkins' storied career.
reviews.author: Carmen Paddock

reviews.text: It is a huge artistic triumph to so cleverly illuminate such a common yet often hard to comprehend condition, and amongst the most evocative and insightful depictions of dementia we've seen on screen...
reviews.author: Emma Simmonds

reviews.text: Manipulations of perspective are smoothly maneuvered by way of Zeller's ingenious simplicity of set design [which] attests to The Father's successful stylistic economy.
reviews.author: Morris Yang

reviews.text: Hopkin's portrayal of a Dementia patient is beautifully acted while simultaneously heartbreaking to watch.
reviews.author: Allison Rose

reviews.text: As we watch, we become painfully aware: this will happen to our parents one day. It will happen to us. Every human life is a progression of seasons.
reviews.author: Brett McCracken

reviews.text: The Father is like the Rashomon of dementia.
reviews.author: Diana Cheng

reviews.text: An absolutely stunning performance in an absolutely heartbreaking movie.
reviews.author: Shawn Edwards

reviews.text: There have been equally effective movies involving Alzheimer's, but none have placed themselves in the mind of the dementia-stricken protagonist as thoroughly as The Father.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: A masterfully made film that is a feast for both the brain and the heart, and a work-out for the tear ducts.
reviews.author: Matt Neal

reviews.text: A masterclass in acting from Hopkins and Colman. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Gianmarco Farfán

reviews.text: A devastating portrait of dementia that hybridizes drama and a subtle, almost Polanskian, horror in one of the best films of the year.
reviews.author: Víctor López G.

reviews.text: There is an unsettling surprise in almost every scene, but Colman's and Hopkin's humanity make sure the audience sticks with the story and is invested in every moment.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: A brutally blunt, yet beautifully honest portrait of a life ending before it is actually over, The Father capitalises on a towering, Oscar-winning performance from Hopkins.
reviews.author: Leigh Paatsch

reviews.text: The Father is very thoughtful and its modest domestic focus is enough to break your heart.
reviews.author: Andrew Kendall

reviews.text: 'The Father' is realistic, compelling look at dementia.
reviews.author: Linda Cook

reviews.text: In inventive and essentially seamless ways, Zeller conveys the unsettling sense of insecurity and vulnerability that comes with a devastating condition like dementia.
reviews.author: Lisa Trifone

reviews.text: The Father has a very precise Resnais quality. But it excises all humanity from a story that is at the same time aiming for the ultra-human, the sickly relatable, and the tragic-but-ordinary.
reviews.author: A.S. Hamrah

reviews.text: Hopkins' masterful performance operates on multiple levels, as the audience isn't sure what's "real" or what's been distorted.
reviews.author: Loren King

reviews.text: The camera becomes an extension of his mind's eye. Faces and places mix and match in an ever-shifting reality, where the only constant is the fallibility of memories. The truth exists between what he remembers and what he's forgotten.
reviews.author: Prahlad Srihari

reviews.text: Emotionally, rationally, and chronologically, The Father whips its viewers around like rag dolls.
reviews.author: Luke Parker

reviews.text: ...a somewhat erratic yet predominantly rewarding endeavor...
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: This is a tragic portrait painted with colors of horror; a study of empathy that tries to put the audience in the mind of a man who is in the process of losing it. [Full review in Portuguese[
reviews.author: Pablo Villaça

reviews.text: Anthony Hopkins is brilliant in forgetting and holding on...
reviews.author: Nandini Ramnath

reviews.text: Sometimes a story like this gets told with a spoonful of genre sugar... "The Father" stays within our unremarkable reality, a world we recognize, until we no longer do.
reviews.author: Rob Gonsalves

reviews.text: The acclaimed actor's struggling retiree marks yet another milestone performance...
reviews.author: Paul M. Bradshaw

reviews.text: The Father presents the rare perspective of someone experiencing memory loss but fails to go beyond the familiar view of a white man with financial means.
reviews.author: Dana Sloane

reviews.text: "The Father" is brutally honest and heartbreaking, making it perhaps the best film about dementia ever seen.
reviews.author: Casey Chong

reviews.text: In Florian Zeller's elegiac The Father, Hopkins gives one of the strongest performances in his storied career, playing a character grappling with his own mortality...
reviews.author: Adam Nayman

reviews.text: What I really appreciated about the film is it suggests there is still a person behind the locked facade of someone with dementia [unlike other movies].
reviews.author: Simon Miraudo

reviews.text: Led by some truly outstanding performances, this one's a celebration of the collective cinematic geniuses that shouldn't be missed.
reviews.author: Ronak Kotecha

reviews.text: As a man helplessly disappearing, Anthony Hopkins is magnificently present.
reviews.author: Shubhra Gupta

reviews.text: Hopkins' performance elevates the material beyond the editing gimmicks and scenery. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Emmanuel Báez

reviews.text: Almost certainly the best of the best-picture nominees.
reviews.author: Sonny Bunch

reviews.text: As a drama, it not only allows Hopkins, in the twilight of his career, to deliver one of his most memorable performances, but also frames it with a clever aesthetic. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: The Father strikes genuine sentiments where it counts.
reviews.author: Matt Conway

reviews.text: "The Father" isn't always convincing, but Hopkins is recurrently fantastic. And watching him turn on a dime from charming and witty to nasty and belligerent is a marvel.
reviews.author: Al Alexander

reviews.text: Childlike vulnerability hasn't been something Hopkins has opened up to show us in a long, long while, but he seems ready for this role, hungry to do it, and you may not be prepared for how deep he goes.
reviews.author: Tim Robey

reviews.text: There is no weak link in The Father.
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: Watching it is like playing "Would You Rather: The Adult Responsibility Edition." Oh, and it ends on a scene that will haunt your brain like you had the word "Amityville" tattooed on your hippocampus. Sounds fun, right?!
reviews.author: Ryan Syrek

reviews.text: [The Father] leans too strongly into the horror tropes, to the point where it seems the film is less about truly understanding the experience of a dementia patient and more about messing with the audience.
reviews.author: Max Weiss

reviews.text: The emotional depths of "The Father" are profound, and the characters bring their memories out vividly.
reviews.author: Asia Frey

reviews.text: In this hall of distorting mirrors Zeller denies us a stable platform where we can stand and make sense of what's really happening in Anthony's life.
reviews.author: John McDonald

reviews.text: An invaluable road map into the mind of the disappearing person you once knew, it gives you the fuel to carry - and care - on.
reviews.author: Jeanmarie Tan

reviews.text: The Father is undoubtedly successful in every way that counts, a deeply affecting film that brings home the horror of Alzheimer's in a way few films dare
reviews.author: Anthony Morris

reviews.text: Deeply sympathetic but never patronising, The Father is a gentle-handed yet powerful film that forces us through Hopkins's extraordinary performance to have an albeit fleeting window into what living with dementia could be like.
reviews.author: Alexandra Heller-Nicholas

reviews.text: Florian Zeller's debut feature film adapting his own play garnered 6 Oscar nominations. With great performances by Olivia Colman and Anthony Hopkins The Father is one of the best films I have seen recently. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alvaro Corujo

reviews.text: There is a beautiful payoff.
reviews.author: tt stern-enzi

reviews.text: There are many reasons to be see this movie-the performances and writing shine-but its biggest success is bringing movie audiences closer to the real horrors of dementia.
reviews.author: Dan Buffa

reviews.text: There's something deeply compassionate and humane at its core. It won't fail to move you.
reviews.author: James Mottram

reviews.text: Anthony Hopkins and Olivia Colman give performances full of dignity and heart while tackling the emotional complexities of dementia. Get several boxes of tissues ready.
reviews.author: Carla Renata

reviews.text: It's a masterwork of both technical filmmaking and soulful drama, packed into a brisk 97 minutes that feels, by design, both like an eternity and like fleeting moments slipping through your fingers like water.
reviews.author: Siddhant Adlakha

reviews.text: Aside from being a superb acting showcase, the defining quality of The Father is how Anthony's constant, maddening state of confusion is shown with such clarity. We see the world as he sees it, only we have the luxury of working out what is going on.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: As overwhelming as The Father can be, its unflinching and unsparing approach is anchored in kindness and compassion - because to truly see something as tough as this is to give it the attention and focus it deserves.
reviews.author: Sarah Ward

reviews.text: It's not scary-horror, but it should scare the stuffing out of anybody who has contemplated their own failing memory. That prospect is far scarier than anything Freddy Krueger ever threw at us.
reviews.author: Paul Byrnes

reviews.text: The Father is an accomplished debut, but it doesn't always live up to the promise of its style and surface complexity with a corresponding profundity or level of insight.
reviews.author: Jason Di Rosso

reviews.text: It's a masterful way to create empathy.
reviews.author: Fletcher Powell

reviews.text: A powerful and compelling drama. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Luis Fernando Galván

reviews.text: The performances by Hopkins and Coleman are outstanding. These two performances are really what make the film so affecting.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: A remarkably powerful film to both admire and be deeply moved by.
reviews.author: Thomas Caldwell

reviews.text: A captivating character-driven drama that uses time and interior design to tell its story beautifully.
reviews.author: Cameron Williams

reviews.text: The Father is a stunning reminder of the power of the medium and how it - and even cinema's most familiar faces - can still surprise.
reviews.author: Kimber Myers

reviews.text: The Father's heart is between [Anthony] Hopkins and [Olivia] Colman, with the two navigating this traumatic exquisiteness to fruition, resulting in a film that's practically a relief on the senses once it has culminated.
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: Anthony Hopkins overwhelms as a man whose mind fails him in confounding and frightening increments.
reviews.author: Andiee Paviour

reviews.text: The Father is a polished piece of work but an unsparing one, offering no false assurances.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: This compelling drama is definitely NOT a feel-good offering. However, it IS deeply moving and enlightening.
reviews.author: Betty Jo Tucker

reviews.text: Disorienting, immersive, infuriating, spectacular.
reviews.author: Michael J. Casey

reviews.text: A deeply compassionate, deeply unnerving portrait of a man suffering from dementia and losing his grip on reality. The empathy machine of cinema has rarely been put to such uncomfortably intimate use.
reviews.author: MaryAnn Johanson

reviews.text: The film is a gripping look at aging and dementia, featuring top notch performances and impressive craft.
reviews.author: Dominic Griffin

reviews.text: Ultimately I'm struck by Anthony Hopkins' courage. At 83, fearlessly taking on this role with such vulnerability.
reviews.author: Eli Glasner

reviews.text: In the potentially dreary role of a devoted daughter dealing with a parent experiencing one of human physiology's saddest realities, Colman helps make the movie an unsentimental heartbreaker.
reviews.author: Anita Katz

reviews.text: A psychological mystery, a truly heart-wrenching drama and a wild emotional ride all at once, The Father is a devastating watch that will haunt you for days.
reviews.author: James Croot

reviews.text: Utterly, profoundly convincing, a powerhouse drama distilled to great purity.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: Anthony Hopkins ... and Olivia Colman ... may each be at the top of their actorly game here, but they both deserve better material.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: The acting is brilliant but the film is totally depressing.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: More than anything, The Father delivers empathy, and an all-too-infrequent opportunity to witness the unseeable through someone else's eyes.
reviews.author: Wm. Steven Humphrey

reviews.text: With the wrong actors, this could have come across as a gimmicky exercise but, as demonstrated in the closing moments, you really grow to care about them both.
reviews.author: Matthew Toomey

reviews.text: The Father is not without its poignant moments. Hopkins' bracing refusal to make the character sympathetic suggests the film that could have been...the gloomy movie turns memory loss into a gimmicky acting exercise...
reviews.author: Rubén Rosario

reviews.text: In his astonishingly assured debut feature, French playwright-turned-director Florian Zeller handles the mental decline of an elderly man with sensitivity and insight.
reviews.author: Christopher Machell

reviews.text: Having Anthony Hopkins and Olivia Colman playing off one another is master class for young actors out there.
reviews.author: Paul McGuire Grimes

reviews.text: [A] masterclass in acting.
reviews.author: Anne Brodie

reviews.text: As a dramatic work The Father is far from perfect, yet there is no denying the fascinating power of Hopkins' performance.
reviews.author: Robert W. Butler

reviews.text: Robbed of truth but not his showy, sparring personality, Anthony isn't an unexpected character from Hopkins, but the performance is a gauntlet and his best in 10 years.
reviews.author: Chance Solem-Pfeifer

reviews.text: For those who tremble in the presence of outstanding performances, The Father will hit like an earthquake. Hopkins and Colman are unspeakably good in their roles.
reviews.author: Thom Ernst

reviews.text: Anthony Hopkins gives a tour de force of a performance that is often a difficult watch but his control of the character, particularly in the film's final heartbreaking moments, as his real and illusory lives intersect, is astonishing.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: Career-crowning work from Hopkins
reviews.author: Jordan Ruimy

reviews.text: A performance of the stature of Hopkins' in The Father doesn't come along often. Let's cherish it while we can.
reviews.author: Cameron Meier

reviews.text: Even by the end, there are no clear answers on any of this. And that is Zeller's most commendable commitment.
reviews.author: David Bax

reviews.text: Zeller's brilliant script and direction is at the core of the film readying a talented cast to give us commandingly powerful story.
reviews.author: Pamela Powell

reviews.text: Hopkins is devastating in frightening dementia drama.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: Bring the tissues, and be prepared to give some long hugs to family members after the end credits roll.
reviews.author: Larry Carroll

reviews.text: "The Father" is ruthless, as it should be, and its reduction of Anthony is complete.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: Florian Zeller enhanced that trippy feeling of the stage play I saw a couple of years ago to even more devastating effect. Beautiful, moving performances by Anthony Hopkins + Olivia Colman.
reviews.author: Ruth Maramis

reviews.text: "The Father" is a touching and empathetic portrait of the painful personal crises of both the patient and his family.
reviews.author: Russ Simmons

reviews.text: A devastating and compassionate portrait about the cognitive decline of a man who has been losing his memory. One of Anthony Hopkins' career-best performances. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rene Sanchez

reviews.text: This is a formidable character study, a moving dissertation on aging, and a tightly wound thriller as well.
reviews.author: Jeff York

reviews.text: In a fine ensemble, the most fabulous bit of casting is pairing the grand Olivia Williams opposite Colman in the same movie. I mean, wasn't it just yesterday that we were all getting the two of them mixed up in our own heads? Bellisimo!
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: Anthony Hopkins at the peak of his powers...
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: The close set and small cast are the ideal building blocks to illustrate the narrowing that so often comes with the end of life, when the world available to us, both physically and socially, grows so small.
reviews.author: Megan Basham

reviews.text: It is Hopkin's performance that really brings it all together. He captures Anthony in a way that feels real, authentic and quite touching.
reviews.author: Micheal Compton

reviews.text: It is emotionally draining, and its trajectory is tragically unavoidable, but it deserves our attention and admiration.
reviews.author: Deirdre Crimmins

reviews.text: I hope Hopkins, who gives one of the best performances of his career, was able to leave this character behind more easily than I could. Take that as both a wish and the deepest of compliments.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: It is painful and honest and brilliant and smart in its orchestration, and in the work by Hopkins and his supporting cast.
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: Watching someone else struggling with a failing memory is a heartbreaking experience, but Hopkins and company make that toil gripping and empathetic. Anthony may not be able to remember what has happened to him, but we will.
reviews.author: Dan Lybarger

reviews.text: In 'The Father', Hopkins and Colman nurture Oscar-worthy performances in one of the year's very best films.
reviews.author: Jeff Mitchell

reviews.text: Illuminated, often thrillingly, by a central performance from Anthony Hopkins that might be the best of his career.
reviews.author: Robert Horton

reviews.text: The Father hits home in multiple ways due to its creative filmmaking and two compelling performances by seasoned actors.
reviews.author: Alex Bentley

reviews.text: One of the best flicks of 2020. (Full Content Review for Parents - Profanity, etc. - also Available)
reviews.author: Jim Judy

reviews.text: The Father - its performances and superior editing skills - makes it one of the most impressive films in the awards race and a must-see film.
reviews.author: Dustin Chase

reviews.text: This isn't about rug pull deception. The goal is instead to put a finger on the waves of clarity and bewilderment Anthony experiences on a daily (sometimes hourly) basis.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: The Father dives deep into the mind, delivering an engaging film that is unsettling, achingly sad, and is strengthened by Zeller's assured narrative.
reviews.author: Mae Abdulbaki

reviews.text: 'The Father' is a painful experience that saddens you. It is, however, one of the best movies of the year. It may lack hope, but it overflows with heart.
reviews.author: Bob Bloom

reviews.text: With the help of a veteran ensemble and excellent technical work, The Father is a master-class on accurately portraying this difficult disease.
reviews.author: Yasmin Kleinbart

reviews.text: "The Father" is in a class of its own. It's a triumph.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: Hopkins is electric here, playing off the always-brilliant Colman and his other solid castmates to create a tragic and indelible portrait of a man desperately clinging to some shred of his identity.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: I liked this, but it's becoming harder to mine new territory with this theme. Sir Tony is always the master of creating a place for his character in the universe of the story.
reviews.author: Patrick McDonald

reviews.text: Anyone who sees The Father will know that Hopkins has given the best performance of the year -- or perhaps, several years.
reviews.author: Eleanor Ringel Cater

reviews.text: "The Father" brilliantly addresses the humanity and frailty in us all, it's singular approach achieving a sense of empathy that proves startling, frighting and unforgettable.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: You feel like you've been through something with "The Father," that it's honest and that it understands how these characters - and perhaps the rest of us - might behave.
reviews.author: Chris Hewitt

reviews.text: In a year full of titanic male performances, Anthony Hopkins ranks high for his seismic turn in "The Father."
reviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski

reviews.text: It's a neat conceit. The trouble is, it stops there.
reviews.author: Kristian M. Lin

reviews.text: It is a credit to the performance that we are never entirely sure how much Anthony understands at any given moment. The line between righteous indignation and self-preservation has been completely blurred.
reviews.author: Matthew Monagle

reviews.text: A corrosive narrative of the death of memory and loss of identity, "The Father" confirms Hopkins' continuing prowess, Colman's growing status and Florian Zeller's arrival as a major film director.
reviews.author: John Wirt

reviews.text: Will be hard for all viewers to watch, some more than others. But it's a lacerating depiction of decline, marked by one of the finest performances ever given by arguably the best actor of our time.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: One of the best films of the year.
reviews.author: Randy Myers

reviews.text: Hopkins' Anthony remains utterly accessible to the audience, never once losing us in the labyrinth of his mind even as he himself stumbles into the gathering darkness.
reviews.author: Bill Newcott

reviews.text: The Father may be the one film that historians pull out to show just why Anthony Hopkins was and is among the very best actors of a generation.
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: It all rings heartbreakingly true.
reviews.author: Mark Meszoros

reviews.text: A thoroughly engrossing and human look at the relationship between a man declining with dementia and the daughter taking care of him.
reviews.author: Christopher Lloyd

reviews.text: "The Father" provides sensitive, superbly compassionate insight into many things, including the fragility of dignity, the ghost prints left by grief and love, and the abiding mysteries of consciousness itself.
reviews.author: Ann Hornaday

reviews.text: It's as if we are in a horror movie... The way it's scored, lit, and the way the camera moves -- we feel like we're not sure and what is not.
reviews.author: Tim Cogshell

reviews.text: "The Father" is the closest we have ever seen on screen of how a person with dementia navigates their new world.
reviews.author: Sarah Knight Adamson

reviews.text: This is the genius of Zeller's labyrinthine filmmaking: in placing the audience in this vulnerable, questioning position, through sound design, camera movement and perspective, we empathize deeply with Anthony's plight.
reviews.author: Katie Walsh

reviews.text: Only a man of his dedication to meticulously observed and fearlessly vulnerable performances could show us Anthony's valiant efforts to stay himself, to stay in charge.
reviews.author: Nell Minow

reviews.text: By design, it's tough to watch at times. Hopkins' performance makes it impossible not to.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: A drama with a mix of sunshine and shadows about a man facing dementia and his daughter struggling to provide him the care he refuses.
reviews.author: Frederic and Mary Ann Brussat

reviews.text: It's a fiendishly inventive approach to the topic at hand, challenging the audience with clever storytelling and frankly astonishing performances.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: Alzheimer's drama has strong language and adult themes.
reviews.author: Kat Halstead

reviews.text: It never finds that level of the fantastic or allows for the kind of magical thinking necessary to escape its dreary reality. Ultimately it wallows in the pathetic. Who needs this?
reviews.author: Vincent Mancini

reviews.text: n a brilliant performance Anthony Hopkins turns this Anthony into a personality empathetic and unnerving.
reviews.author: Alci Rengifo

reviews.text: Simply superb. A devastating and claustrophobic horror story that plays out - through all those doors - like a grim farce.
reviews.author: Sarah Cartland

reviews.text: While the movie will be touted mainly for Anthony Hopkins' fantastic performance, this complexly structured project is to be lauded all around.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: A very accurate portrayal of how frustrating it can be not just for the family but for the person who is losing his or her faculties.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: [A] different type of psychological horror story ... told entirely from the perspective of an elderly man with dementia ... a harrowing ride ... of uncertainty and confusion, anchored by outstanding performances from Anthony Hopkins and Olivia Colman.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: A haunting, heartbreaking film, made even more so by the towering performances of its two leads.
reviews.author: Mattie Lucas

reviews.text: The film features Hopkins as a man with dementia, and the actor takes viewers on a compelling journey through shifting realities.
reviews.author: Noah Gittell

reviews.text: Florian Zeller's drama is a brilliant exploration of dementia, pain, and vulnerability.
reviews.author: Josh Flanders

reviews.text: The film uses these abrupt changes to show how frustrating and terrifying memory loss and dementia are. It's a cinematic conceit cleverly used to break away from the stagebound origins,
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: The sort of thing that gives year-end middlebrow prestige cinema a good name.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: It's a head-spinning masterpiece, and Hopkins tops himself as an actor.
reviews.author: Tim Appelo

reviews.text: To see Hopkins play all these ever-fluctuating turns of mood is riveting... Yet "The Father" often feels like a clinical puzzle to work out.
reviews.author: Jake Coyle

reviews.text: there have been few better attempts on screen to capture dementia, punctuated by a staggering performance from Anthony Hopkins, a brilliant cherry on top of the 83-year-old actor's extraordinary career.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: [The Father] gives Anthony Hopkins a role designed to nearly break your heart: a role full of anger and displacement and uncertainty but, also, flashes of humor, a sprightly fullness of life. Reminders of who this man once was.
reviews.author: K. Austin Collins

reviews.text: It's a rising nightmare, exquisitely structured, staged and performed.
reviews.author: Ricardo Gallegos

reviews.text: Masterful and agonizing, The Father is a gorgeously crafted film about a doomed arrangement entered into with love, even though it can only end in tragedy.
reviews.author: Alison Willmore

reviews.text: At some points Hopkins seems almost uninhabited, his eyes dropping to the floor in search of something that's no longer there.
reviews.author: Kurt Loder

reviews.text: Anthony Hopkins delivers a master class in acting as a once-brilliant man losing his mental faculties to the plague of dementia. First-time director Florian Zeller turns his modern "King Lear" of a play into essential cinema.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: The mainspring of "The Father," onscreen, is the presence of Hopkins-an actor at the frightening summit of his powers, portraying a man brought pitifully low. The irony is too rare to resist.
reviews.author: Anthony Lane

reviews.text: The Father is an excellent movie but it's not a lot of fun to watch, especially for those with first-hand experience in this area.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: Zeller, making an impressive feature debut, employs a sort of dream logic of the everyday and the mundane in his storytelling.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: It's impossible to imagine what going through dementia must feel like, but Zeller's approach, paired with Hopkins' masterful performance, is perhaps one of the more convincing and arresting attempts at doing so.
reviews.author: Steve Katz

reviews.text: Playing someone with a disease like Alzheimer's is always risky for a performer, because it's easy to get so bogged down in playing the symptoms that the character itself can get lost. Hopkins plays a man first and foremost, to the film's great benefit.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: What might have been predictable or sentimental in other hands becomes startling in the film's approach, as well as beguiling, unsparing, terribly moving and occasionally very funny. Mr. Hopkins is the master of it all.
reviews.author: Joe Morgenstern

reviews.text: The Father is absolutely brutal, particularly for those who have cared for a loved one enduring dementia. I could barely stomach the movie. An entertaining night out it is not. But we do look to art for truths, even ones we'd rather not confront.
reviews.author: Kyle Smith

reviews.text: Olivia Colman is perfect as his wounded daughter Anne.
reviews.author: Neely Swanson

reviews.text: Zeller, working from his own acclaimed 2012 French-language play Le Pére, is able to turn devastating illness into a kind of disjointed poetry - and one still threaded with real emotional resonance...
reviews.author: Leah Greenblatt

reviews.text: Captures the terrifying sensation of not remembering and not understanding the people and places around us, and the helplessness of having to have your reality explained to you.
reviews.author: Alonso Duralde

reviews.text: It's an astounding, charred turn by Hopkins-a reminder, if anyone needs one, that he's one of the greats of his generation.
reviews.author: Andy Crump

reviews.text: Writer/director Florian Zeller, adapting his prize-winning, 2012 French play of the same name with the help of the legendary Christopher Hampton, has pulled off a dazzling feat here.
reviews.author: Christy Lemire

reviews.text: The film's final embrace is a quietly astounding vision of grace in solitude, and it harks back to that opening aria, with its invocation of eternal winter and the unheard rejoinder that follows: " 'Tis Love, 'tis Love, 'tis Love that has warm'd us."
reviews.author: Justin Chang

reviews.text: Narratives like this are seldom told subtly - what's subtle about dementia? - but The Father's nuances and cannily told perspectives are keenly observed in ways that stories like this need to be.
reviews.author: Kayleigh Donaldson

reviews.text: At once stupendously effective and profoundly upsetting, "The Father" might be the first movie about dementia to give me actual chills.
reviews.author: Jeannette Catsoulis

reviews.text: Truly, Florian has absolutely shown his might as a filmmaker, with his cast deserving every plaudit they get.
reviews.author: Jenny Desborough

reviews.text: While the drama goes to some disturbing places (including incidents of elder abuse), at its core it is very much about love and the power of empathy.
reviews.author: Brian Truitt

reviews.text: What Zeller has so remarkably done here is to take any semblance of theatricality from this story and play it in another medium where it is actually enhanced.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: Hopkins makes an indelible impression in the fading twilight grappling with an invisible foe that's taking pieces of him away. It's the ravages of senility by way of Shakespeare.
reviews.author: Neil Pond

reviews.text: Hopkins is a force of nature in The Father, playing a role that demands a full emotional and intellectual scope.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: Hopkins makes himself transparent. He lets us see both who this man was and what he is now.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: Hopkins' final tearful moments in THE FATHER are as far removed from Hannibal Lecter as anyone could imagine. It is a tribute to the man's incredible talent to move an audience in very different ways.
reviews.author: David Kaplan

reviews.text: Do not be deterred by the subject matter. Instead, seize the opportunity to watch Hopkins, Colman and the rest work together to bring Zeller's important story to the silver screen.
reviews.author: Jeanne Kaplan

reviews.text: Featuring phenomenal central performances from Hopkins and Colman, The Father is an innovative and hugely poignant portrayal of dementia.
reviews.author: Nicola Austin

reviews.text: "... a showcase for Hopkins' extraordinary talent with line readings."
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: The Father mainly is a vehicle for a performance from Anthony Hopkins for the ages.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: Anthony Hopkins gives an amazing performance in this delirious look at dementia.
reviews.author: Leigh Monson

reviews.text: With mesmerising performances from Hopkins and Colman, The Father excels in creating a compelling and heartbreaking narrative. Florian Zeller's film capably conveys the quiet hell of the disease, while never losing the human touch. A must-see film.
reviews.author: Adam Solomons

reviews.text: Among the best narrative films about dementia in memory.
reviews.author: Harvey S. Karten

reviews.text: All of this works so impressively because of the master class in acting presented by Anthony Hopkins as Anthony and Olivia Colman as Anne.
reviews.author: Diane Carson

reviews.text: while the actors who support Hopkins are all top notch, especially Colman's infinitely patient and loving Anne, it is the production itself which showcases his performance like a flawless diamond...a dazzling filmmaking debut
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: This empathetic portrayal of the subtle disorientation of dementia is brilliantly acted and emotionally devastating...
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: A fully immersive experience with the frustrations of dementia.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: An unforgettable, powerful film with colosal performances. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Nestor Bentancor

reviews.text: Uncompromisingly moving and emotional... thanks to two extraordinary artists who offer charismatic and fully expressive performances. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: ... it's like having Bergman and Haneke crossing styles.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: Astutely adapting his acclaimed play, Florian Zeller makes a breathtaking directorial debut with his wrenchingly perceptive look at advancing dementia and the toll it takes on those close to the afflicted.
reviews.author: Alan Jones

reviews.text: The Father removes the voyeuristic boundary between the observer and the observed and chucks us into the thick of it.
reviews.author: Matt Oakes

reviews.text: Hopkins and Colman are sure to garner accolades for their performances exposing dementia in detail from Writer/Director Florian Zeller's mind-bending, personal, point of view.

reviews.text: A very inventive and accomplished debut for Zeller: an awesomely difficult subject beautifully, movingly brought to the cinema screen.

reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: An execution that is as brilliant as it is simple. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Andrea G. Bermejo

reviews.author: A.A. Dowd

reviews.text: Florian Zeller is telling not so much a story about dementia but rather goes for a visceral and vicarious depiction of that, making for something wholly original and hauntingly beautiful

reviews.text: The Father approximates the dislocation of its main character's mind with a frighteningly slippery ease.

reviews.text: The movie's best features are these deeply moving performances and the unusual point of view.

reviews.text: ...stunning, phenomenal... Pick your superlative.
reviews.author: Mark Demetrius

reviews.text: A transcendent film that presents a remarkably ingenious depiction of the crippling disorientation of dementia. The end result is as breathtaking as it is devastating.

reviews.text: Anthony Hopkins and Olivia Colman deliver powerhouse performances in The Father.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: Just as in The Two Popes, last year, Sir Anthony delivers a master class in acting. You can't take your eyes off of him.

reviews.text: Now that's how you properly exploit a movie star persona.
reviews.author: Katie Rife

reviews.text: The Father is a fascinating portrait of a tragic fate that that affects families as much as those who suffer from it directly, and which, terrifyingly, awaits so many.

reviews.text: Florian Zeller skillfully adapts his stage play to paint a sorrowful portrait of an elderly parent suffering from dementia.

reviews.text: The results are both mind-bending and heart-rending.
reviews.author: Kate Taylor

reviews.text: "Whether or not these performances will connect with audiences will depend almost entirely on the individual's tolerance for intensely upsetting, psychologically immersive tragedy."
reviews.author: Alex Hudson

reviews.text: Hopkins is fully committed to his character, and Zeller's work is just as committed to him.
reviews.author: Andrew Parker

reviews.text: Scenes, sequences, and arcs fray at the edges until they snake in on themselves.
reviews.author: Matt Cipolla

reviews.text: Once The Father has you, it's hard to fall out of its momentum.
reviews.author: Karl Delossantos

reviews.text: Sort of like how Requiem For a Dream put viewers in the experience of a drug addict, it's not a pleasant experience but it's invigorating to see how cinema can capture human experiences that mere words can't convey.

reviews.text: Playing out over an unspecified amount of time yet staying in only a couple of apartments, the film corners you, becoming smaller and more intimate as time goes on.

reviews.text: It's a tough watch but a structurally powerful piece of storytelling with a powerhouse performance at its center, matched by a supporting ensemble that doesn't have a weak link.

reviews.text: By messing with the geography of the apartment and the identities of its characters, The Father makes us see and digest and experience the frighteningly unsystematic loss of mental control.

reviews.text: The Father is an act of understanding, radical in its toughness and its generous artistry.

reviews.text: The Father takes a bracingly insightful, subtle and nuanced look at encroaching dementia and the toll it takes on those in close proximity to the afflicted.

reviews.text: No one but Hopkins and Colman could play these roles. The Father is a testament to their talents and proof that they are two of the best actors we have.

reviews.text: All the actors in "The Father" are vivid (Colman brings her role a loving vulnerability that warms you), but Hopkins is flat-out stunning.

reviews.text: For those who can stomach it, it'll stay with you, for longer than you might like. I know it will stay with me.
reviews.author: Benjamin Lee

synopsis: Anthony (Academy Award Winner, Anthony Hopkins) is 80, mischievous, living defiantly alone and rejecting the carers that his daughter, Anne (Academy Award and Golden Globe Winner, Olivia Colman), encouragingly introduces. Yet help is also becoming a necessity for Anne; she can't make daily visits anymore and Anthony's grip on reality is unraveling. As we experience the ebb and flow of his memory, how much of his own identity and past can Anthony cling to? How does Anne cope as she grieves the loss of her father, while he still lives and breathes before her? THE FATHER warmly embraces real life, through loving reflection upon the vibrant human condition; heart-breaking and uncompromisingly poignant -- a movie that nestles in the truth of our own lives.
